SIKADUR®-32 LP: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikadur®-32 LP, September 2026, Version 02.05 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/s/sikadur_-32_lp.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikadur®-32 LP where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2026, Version 02.05).
1.2 Product description. Sikadur®-32 LP is a moisture tolerant, structural, two part bonding agent, based on a combination of epoxy resins and special fillers, designed with a longer potlife or working time for use at higher temperatures, between +20 °C and +40 °C.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikadur®-32 LP may only be used by experienced professionals. As a corrosion protection to reinforcement as per EN1504.
    - Suitable for cathodic control (Principle 9, method 9.1 EN 1504-9)
    - Suitable for control of anodic areas (Principle 11, method 11.2 EN 1504-9)
    - Concrete elements (including bonding fresh to hardened concrete)
    - Hard natural stone
    - Ceramics, fibre-cement
    - Monotop Repair Mortars, Bricks, Masonry, Render
    - Steel, Iron, Aluminium
    - Wood
    - Polyester / fibreglass and epoxy resin materials
    - Glass
    As a structural bonding agent and adhesive for:
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.7.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikadur®-32 LP
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Epoxy bonding agent and Reinforcement Corrosion Protection
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports.
    - AS/NZS 4020:2018 Potable Water Approved
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN1504: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Uses (p.1).
    - EN 1504-9: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Uses (p.1).
    - AS/NZS 4020:2018: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - ASTM C579: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - ASTM D 695-95: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in compression (p.2).
    - DIN EN ISO 178: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Flexural-strength (p.2); Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in flexure (p.2).
    - ISO 527: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in tension (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strain at break (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN ISO 4624: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 12188: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 1770: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Coefficient of thermal expansion (p.2).
    - EN 1799: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Sag flow (p.3).
    - EN ISO 9514: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Pot Life (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Easy to mix and apply
    - Suitable for dry and damp concrete substrates
    - Very good adhesion to most construction materials
    - High bond strength
    - Hardens without shrinkage
    - Different coloured components (for mixing control)
    - No primer needed
    - High initial and ultimate mechanical strengths
    - Impermeable to liquids and water vapour
    - Good chemical resistance
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Epoxy resin and selected fillers
    - Colour: Component A: white; Component B: dark grey; Components A+B mixed: concrete grey
    - Density: 1.4 ± 0.1 kg/l (component A+B mixed) (at +23 °C)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: ~2100 N/mm² (14 days at +23 °C) (ASTM D 695-95)
    - Modulus of elasticity in flexure: ~2600 N/mm²(14 days at +23 °C) (DIN EN ISO 178)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~2750 N/mm² (14 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile strain at break: 1.0 ± 0.1 % (14 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Shrinkage: Hardens without shrinkage.
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 11.4 × 10⁻⁵ 1/K (Temp. range +23 °C - +60 °C) (EN 1770)

2.12 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 3 lt (A & B) kit; 18 lt (A & B) kit
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Always refer to packaging.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2026, Version 02.05) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality.
    - Hardened mortar and concrete must be older than 28 days (depending on any minimal strength requirements). Verify the substrate strength by testing (concrete, masonry, natural stone). The substrate surface (all types) must be clean, dry or mat damp (no standing water) and free from contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, existing surface treatments and coatings etc.
    - Steel substrates must be de-rusted to a condition similar to Sa 2.5. The substrate must be sound and all loose or friable particles must be removed.
3.3 Substrate preparation.
    - Concrete, mortar, stone and brick
    - Concrete and other hardened mineral substrates must be prepared by suitable means such as high pressure water jetting and / or blast cleaning, in order to obtain surfaces that are sound, clean, dry or mat damp (no standing water) and free from any cement laitance, ice, grease, oils, old coatings or other surface treatments. Any loose or friable particles must also be removed to achieve a contaminant free and open textured surface.
    - Steel
    - Steel surface must be cleaned and prepared thoroughly to an acceptable quality standard equivalent to Sa 2.5 i.e. normally by blast cleaning and then removing any dust by vacuum. Avoid dew point conditions.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2026, Version 02.05) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Part A : Part B = 2 : 1 by weight or volume
    - Consumption: ~1.3 kg/m² per mm of thickness. This figure is theoretical and does not allow for any additional material due to surface porosity, surface profile, variations in level or wastage etc.
    - Layer thickness: ~1 mm max.
    - Sag flow: On vertical surfaces it is non-sag up to 1.0 mm thickness. (EN 1799)
4.3 Pot Life.
    | Temperature | Potlife* | Open time |
    | +20 °C | ~145 minutes | ~270 minutes |
    | +30 °C | ~55 minutes | ~240 minutes |
    | +40 °C | ~35 minutes | ~120 minutes |
    Test method printed: (EN ISO 9514)
    Note printed: *200 g The potlife begins when Parts A+B are mixed. It is shorter at high temperatures and longer at low temperatures. The greater the quantity mixed, the shorter the potlife. To obtain longer workability at high temperatures, the mixed adhesive may be divided into smaller quantities. Another method is to chill Parts A+B before mixing (not below +5 °C).
4.4 Mixing - Pre-batched units. Mix components A+B together for at least 3 minutes with a mixing spindle attached to a slow speed electric drill (max. 300 rpm) until the material becomes smooth in consistency and a uniform grey colour. Avoid aeration while mixing. Then, pour the whole mix into a clean container and stir again for approx. 1 more minute at low speed to keep air entrapment at a minimum. Mix only that quantity which can be used within its potlife.
4.5 Application method / tools.
    - Apply the mixed Sikadur®-32 LP to the prepared surface by brush, roller, spray or with a trowel, and ensure uniform and complete coverage. On hardened concrete substrates mechanically prepared to receive fresh concrete, always apply by brush and work the material well into the substrate.
    - Place the fresh concrete whilst the Sikadur®-32 LP layer is still ‘tacky’. If the material becomes glossy and loses tackiness, apply a fresh coat with additional Sikadur®-32 LP and proceed.
4.6 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Sika® Colma Cleaner immediately after use. Hardened material can only be mechanically removed.
4.7 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Sikadur® resins are formulated to have low creep under permanent loading. However due to the creep behaviour of all polymer materials under load, when using adhesive for structural applications, the long term structural design load must account for creep. Generally the long term structural design load must be lower than 20−25 % of the failure load. A structural engineer must be consulted for design calculations for specific structural applications.
    - When using multiple units during application, do not mix the following unit until the previous one has been used in order to avoid a reduction in workability and handling time.
    - For heavy components positioned vertically or overhead, provide temporary support.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Material temperature. +20 °C min. / +40 °C max.
5.3 Ambient air temperature. +20 °C min. / +40 °C max.
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation. Steel substrate temperature during application must be at least +3 °C above dew point.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +20 °C min. / +40 °C max.
5.6 Substrate moisture content. Substrate must be dry or mat damp (no standing water); Brush the material well into the substrate
5.7 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: Curing time | Curing temperature; +23 °C | +30 °C | +40 °C; 1 day | ~10 N/mm² | ~20 N/mm² | ~30 N/mm²; 3 days | ~14 N/mm² | ~24 N/mm² | ~41 N/mm²; 7 days | ~34 N/mm² | ~38 N/mm² | ~52 N/mm²; 28 days | ~39 N/mm² | ~43 N/mm² | ~56 N/mm² (ASTM C579)
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: ~2100 N/mm² (14 days at +23 °C) (ASTM D 695-95)
    - Flexural-strength: Curing time | Curing temperature; +23 °C | +30 °C | +40 °C; 1 day | − | − | ~18 N/mm²; 3 days | ~21 N/mm² | ~20 N/mm² | ~30 N/mm²; 7 days | ~24 N/mm² | ~28 N/mm² | ~36 N/mm²; 14 days | ~38 N/mm² | ~38 N/mm² | ~42 N/mm² (DIN EN ISO 178)
    - Modulus of elasticity in flexure: ~2600 N/mm²(14 days at +23 °C) (DIN EN ISO 178)
    - Tensile strength: Curing time | Curing temperature; +23 °C | +30 °C | +40 °C; 1 day | − | − | ~11 N/mm²; 3 days | ~13 N/mm² | ~16 N/mm² | ~18 N/mm²; 7 days | ~20 N/mm² | ~18 N/mm² | ~22 N/mm²; 14 days | ~22 N/mm² | ~24 N/mm² | ~25 N/mm² (ISO 527)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~2750 N/mm² (14 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile strain at break: 1.0 ± 0.1 % (14 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: Curing time | Substrate | Curing | Adhesion; temperature | strength; 7 days | Concrete dry | +23 °C | > 3 N/mm² *; 7 days | Concrete | +23 °C | > 3 N/mm² *; moist; 1 day | Steel | +23 °C | ~8 N/mm²; 3 days | Steel | +23 °C | ~12 N/mm²; 3 days | Steel | +30 °C | ~13 N/mm²; 3 days | Steel | +40 °C | ~15 N/mm² (EN ISO 4624, EN 1542, EN 12188)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 11.4 × 10⁻⁵ 1/K (Temp. range +23 °C - +60 °C) (EN 1770)
    - Heat deflection temperature: Curing time | Curing | HDT; temperature; 7 days | +23 °C | +49 °C (ISO 75)
    - Sag flow: On vertical surfaces it is non-sag up to 1.0 mm thickness. (EN 1799)
    - Pot Life: Temperature | Potlife* | Open time; +20 °C | ~145 minutes | ~270 minutes; +30 °C | ~55 minutes | ~240 minutes; +40 °C | ~35 minutes | ~120 minutes (EN ISO 9514)
5.8 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.9 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikadur®-32 LP, September 2026, Version 02.05, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/s/sikadur_-32_lp.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikadur 32 LP part B, version 12/10/2021, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/k/Sikadur%2032LP%20Part%20B%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikadur 32 LP Part A, version 27/09/2022, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/Sikadur%2032%20LP%20Part%20A.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-32 LP Part B, version 14/12/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/4/sds-sikadur-32-lppartb.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-32 LP Part A, version 14/12/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/sds-sikadur-32-lpparta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
